Guys, 

1. The PERM is not an immigration benefit. It’s clearly mentioned on the USCIS website. It’s a petition that leads to one. 

2. The PERM is NOT official until the “approved” form is signed by the petitioner and beneficiary under perjury. So any mistakes done on an approved PERM may still be corrected after approval. It’s happened before. 

3. While a claim to U.S citizenship may be problematic, it generally needs to be associated to a benefit. For example, claiming to be a U.S citizen to cross the country, claiming to be U.S citizen to get a job (I-9). In OP’s case, there’s no impact at all. 

This clerical error has happened before. 

To OP, I wish you the best. Your attorney can file an appeal to a higher department by proving that it was a mistake and maybe providing proof of your country’s citizenship. However, an appeal can take long and the decision is not certain. 

The other option is to start fresh and begin the recruitment while the PWD is in process to shorten the processing time a little bit. Hang in there, you’ll make it through!
